newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends up slightly vs US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends up slightly vs US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up slightly in inactive trade on Monday at 8.2902 to the U.S. dollar against 8.2906 last Friday, dealers said.
They added, however, that demand for the yuan would remain firm, helped by dollar sales by exporters.
The weighted average price on Friday was 8.2905.

On Monday, the yuan held near the key resistance level of 8.2900. It opened down at an intraday low of 8.2909 and traded within a range of 8.2902 and 8.2905 for most of the session, hitting a high of 8.2900.
"Demand for the yuan increased when the currency was below the 8.2900 level as many investors believe it will breach that price in the short term," one dealer said.
"The yuan failed to stand firm at the resistance level of 8.2900 today, but bullish sentiment will push the yuan up further in the near future," he said.
"If the yuan firms above that price, it will have no difficulty breaching a 26-month closing high of 8.2892," another dealer said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move around the 8.2900 level on Tuesday.
The yuan closed slightly higher at 7.0799 from 7.1005 against 100 Japanese yen and little changed at 1.0702 from 1.0700 against the Hong Kong dollar.
